newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Thousands pay final farewell to Loubna in Morocco.
newsitem.headline: Thousands pay final farewell to Loubna in Morocco.

text.p: Thousands of Moroccans crowded a Tangier cemetery on Sunday to bury a young girl -- apparent victim of a child molester -- found dead in the basement of a Brussels garage five years after she disappeared.

"We are here to say no to violence against children and for peace between peoples," said a mourner at the mosque where the body of Loubna Benaissa lay in a simple coffin before being taken to the Martyrs Cemetery just outside Tangier, hometown of the girl's family.

The body of Loubna, aged nine when she disappeared in August 1992 while shopping for her mother, was discovered on Wednesday in a steel trunk in the basement of a garage in the Brussels suburb of Ixelles where she lived.
Patrick Derochette, a convicted child molester who worked at the garage, has been charged with the abduction, rape of a child under 10 and illegal imprisonment leading to death.

The discovery of the body shocked Belgians, already reeling from paedophile scandals. Loubna brought to five the number of young girls found dead in Belgium since last August when another convicted paedophile, Marc Dutroux, was arrested.
The official Moroccan news agency MAP said up to 30,000 people were at the funeral, punctuated by the wailing of mourners and verses recited from the Koran.
Yves de Jonghe d'Ardoye, mayor of the Brussels suburb where the family lived, told MAP:

"I have come to Morocco to pay hommage to the Benaissa family and all the members of the Moroccan community who live in the commune which I represent, for the courage and dignified behaviour which they have shown during this harsh test."
On Saturday some 20,000 people in Belgium attended a ceremony for Loubna before her body was flown to Morocco.

"My little Loubna. Our little Loubna, because you have become everyone's child. The child of a whole country," Nabela Beanaissa, 17, the dead girl's sister, said at that ceremony. "Today pain unites us. Tomorrow I hope it will be love."
"Loubna, at last I can say goodbye to you. Goodbye in the name of all who love you," she said.
Before the burial, Loubna's body lay in a simple coffin in the main Mohamed V mosque in central Tangier for Moslem prayers for the dead.

The coffin was then placed in a white ambulance for a slow funeral procession to the cemetery. Thousands of people quietly followed on foot, including Tangier Governor Allal Essaadaoui, Belgian Ambassador Marc Van Rysseleerghe and members of the Moroccan parliament.
